policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'and with the emerods', a single term for the same affliction that both readings name: qere ובטחרים (tumors/hemorrhoids) and ketiv ובעפלים (swellings/tumors) are synonymous euphemism pairs, so the English word cannot show which was before the translators. The only note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, tumors. Or, plague boils'), which concerns English wording and never decides a reading. No italicized supply bears on the choice. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV reads 'another man shall lie with her'. 'Lie with' is the plain lexical rendering of the qere ישכבנה (שכב, to lie down with); the ketiv ישגלנה (שגל) means to ravish or violate, which the ASV does not say, here or in a note. The two readings differ in English-visible force, not merely in spelling, and the ASV wording matches the qere, so the ASV distinguishes this reading. No mapped textual_variant note qualifies it.
